title: Using AI to build a card game: I needed a test for cards that looked finished but weren't
author: Niroooooo
selftext:
I'm building Nexus Breach, a browser card game, with AI tools involved in the code, art, sound and music.



One problem with this kind of project is that a card can look finished well before it works. It has a name, art and rules text. None of that means the engine knows what to do when someone plays it.



Card effects in the game have to be connected to implementations, and there are tests around that coverage. I also keep the rules engine separate from database calls so I can test a combat change without setting up a multiplayer room.



That still doesn't prove the game is balanced. A test can show that a card does what I specified while missing that the thing I specified is a bad idea.



For anyone else building games this way: what do you test automatically, and what do you still have to catch by playing?



If you want to see the project, the tutorial is here: [https://play.nexusbreach.com/tutorial](https://play.nexusbreach.com/tutorial)



No account needed for that. The full game is free-to-play with paid expansions.
